rules.rationale: Chalcogenide anions raised refractive index in dielectric source; polarizability raises phonon DOS peaks.
Post-transition main-group heavy elements raised source objective; high Z raises phonon frequencies.
Moderate concentration balances polarizability and bonding complexity.
Mid mean Z covers chalcogenides and post-transition heavy elements.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers chalcogenide and heavy-element polarity effects from dielectric refractive index; fails if phonon peaks are dominated by light-element modes.

rules.rationale: Oxides dominate the target pool but are typically covalent, giving low-lying phonon peaks.
Light nonmetals lowered source objective; low Z lowers phonon frequencies.
Binary compositions have few bonding modes, reducing peak intensity.
Low mean Z covers light nonmetals and binaries.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses the low-confidence halogen and quinary-seinery source relations and adds oxide covalency; fails if oxides carry high-lying peaks.

lesson: Across four development seeds, the chalcogenide polarity skill led the counter-hypothesis on both AUC and final best, though with high variance: two seeds reached near-perfect performance while two others were poor. This suggests the polarity mechanism is the right direction but the skill is brittle, so I kept it with the same rules and parameters.
revision_summary: Retained the chalcogenide polarity skill and replaced the halide and quinary-seinery counter-hypothesis with an oxide covalency counter-hypothesis. The new counter-hypothesis keeps the low-Z and binary rules but replaces halide with oxide, which dominates the target pool and is typically covalent, giving low-lying phonon peaks. Both skills use two-to-four mechanistically interpretable rules, and neither uses placeholder keys or target outcomes.
